title: Session capture and chain-of-custody playbook for model-access incidents
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the required actions, tools, and artifacts for capturing privileged session activity and preserving chain-of-custody when a model-serving or model-access incident is suspected or confirmed. It is focused on incidents where an account, service identity, or session may have accessed model weights, KV caches, or customer request data in a way that requires forensic preservation and potential regulatory evidence.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood runtime variants (Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private deployments).
- Covers human and machine sessions that interact with model-serving control plane or data plane (session-proxy, admin-console, runtime shell access, model-pull operations).
- Does not replace legal/HR review for internal misconduct; legal hold instructions must be followed if requested.

Goals and SLOs
- Evidence collection started: within 2 hours of incident detection.
- Initial preservation snapshot copied to secure evidence-bucket: within 6 hours.
- Complete chain-of-custody manifest produced: within 24 hours.
- Tamper-evident storage (immutable bucket + WORM) used for final evidence retention.

Key services and artifacts (names used in examples)
- redwood-runtime: main inference runtime (per-region).
- session-proxy: privileged session gateway for operator shells and debug sessions.
- audit-collector: log aggregation (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch).
- evidence-bucket: S3 bucket with object-lock enabled (s3://redwood-evidence-prod).
- identity-service: OIDC / SCIM provider and entitlement store.
- kv-cache-store: model KV cache store (Redis or remote cache).

Incident classification that triggers this playbook
1. Unauthorized model pull (unexpected model download to non-approved node).
2. Suspicious session that executed model-inspection or memory-dump commands.
3. High-volume extraction of embeddings or reranking results traced to a single credential.
4. Detection of unexplained access to customer request payloads through runtime logs.

Roles & responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC) — security oncall: coordinates collection and escalation.
- Forensics Lead — security forensics engineer: performs deep collection, verifies integrity.
- Runtime Owner — eng-serving-runtime: provides node-level access and runtime artifacts.
- Customer Success Lead — customer-success: communicates with affected customers per security policy.
- Legal / Compliance: instructs on legal hold and external disclosure.
- SRE — eng-sre: assists with log exports, snapshotting volumes, and cluster preservation.

Prerequisites and permissions
- Evidence collection role (evidence-collector) with scoped read access to audit-collector and s3 write to evidence-bucket.
- Immutable bucket policy and object-lock turned on for s3://redwood-evidence-prod.
- Playbook runner has access to the evidentiary manifest template (see below).

Step-by-step procedure (high-level)
1) Triage and contain (IC, Runtime Owner)
   - Mark the incident ticket with severity and tags: incident:security, evidence-required.
   - If a live malicious session is detected, terminate or isolate the session via session-proxy: `redwoodctl session terminate --id <session-id>`.
   - If model-serving nodes are at risk, cordon affected nodes (Dedicated/Private) or route traffic away (Hosted).

2) Live capture (Forensics Lead, SRE)
   - Capture session metadata from session-proxy (timestamp, src IP, user, session-id, commands executed). Example query (OpenSearch DSL):
     POST _search
     {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term":{"session_id":"<session-id>"}}]}}}

   - Export relevant audit logs from audit-collector for the time window [T-1h, T+1h] where T is detection time. Example Splunk/KQL: 
     index=redwood_audit sourcetype=session-proxy session_id=<session-id> | table _time user src_ip command

   - Snapshot runtime process memory if legal-approved and safe: `gcore -o /tmp/core-<pid> <pid>` executed only with Forensics Lead and Runtime Owner present.

3) Disk & KV cache preservation (Runtime Owner, SRE)
   - Create filesystem snapshot or EBS volume snapshot for affected nodes. AWS CLI example: `aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --description "incident-<id>-runtime-snapshot"`
   - Export KV cache keys metadata (do NOT dump full customer PII unless authorized). Example Redis RDB dump command: `redis-cli --rdb /tmp/dump-<id>.rdb` then copy to evidence-bucket.

4) Evidence packaging and manifest (Forensics Lead)
   - Upload collected artifacts to evidence-bucket in a path that includes incident id and UTC timestamp: `s3://redwood-evidence-prod/incidents/INC-2026-045/`
   - Generate chain-of-custody manifest (see template below) and sign it with the forensics lead PGP key or internal signing service.

5) Verification & sealing (IC, Forensics Lead, Legal)
   - Verify each uploaded object checksum (SHA256) and record entries in the manifest.
   - Apply object-lock governance for final retention window as instructed by Legal.

6) Post-collection analysis & reporting (Forensics Lead, Runtime Owner)
   - Correlate session commands with runtime trace logs, model pull audit events, and network egress logs.
   - Produce a forensics summary for the incident ticket and attach the manifest.

Chain-of-custody manifest (text table template)
- Manifest fields (plain text key:value lines)
  - incident_id: INC-2026-045
  - collected_by: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
  - role: Forensics Lead
  - collection_time_utc: 2026-05-03T14:32:00Z
  - artifact_id: runtime-snapshot-vol-0123456789abcdef0
  - artifact_type: ebs-snapshot
  - artifact_location: s3://redwood-evidence-prod/incidents/INC-2026-045/runtime-snapshot-vol-0123456789abcdef0.snap
  - sha256: 3b2f9e...
  - custody_transfers: [2026-05-03T16:02:00Z|aisha.patel@redwood.ai|uploaded], [2026-05-04T09:12:00Z|legal@redwood.ai|reviewed]
  - signature: -----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----...

Example manifest as lines (for copying into the evidence bag):
```
incident_id=INC-2026-045
collected_by=aisha.patel@redwood.ai
role=forensics-lead
collection_time_utc=2026-05-03T14:32:00Z
artifact_id=runtime-snapshot-vol-0123456789abcdef0
artifact_type=ebs-snapshot
artifact_location=s3://redwood-evidence-prod/incidents/INC-2026-045/runtime-snapshot-vol-0123456789abcdef0.snap
sha256=3b2f9e2b1a5f4c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d
custody_transfers=2026-05-03T16:02:00Z|aisha.patel@redwood.ai|uploaded;2026-05-04T09:12:00Z|legal@redwood.ai|reviewed
signature=PGP_SIG_PLACEHOLDER
```

Preservation & retention policy (recommended defaults)
- Incident evidence (non-PII): retain 2 years in evidence-bucket with object-lock governance.
- Incident evidence (PII or regulated data): hold per Legal instructions; typical regulatory default = 7 years.
- Short-term analysis copies: ephemeral copies in secure analysis project for up to 30 days, then either destroyed or moved to evidence-bucket.

Tamper-evidence checklist
- Every uploaded artifact has a recorded SHA256 checksum in the manifest.
- Each custody transfer is recorded with timestamp and operator identity.
- Evidence-bucket uses object-lock (governance or compliance mode) and server-side encryption (SSE-KMS).
- Audit logs that show who accessed the evidence-bucket are preserved separately in audit-collector.

Cross-environment specifics
- Hosted API (multi-tenant control plane):
  - Do not pull full request payloads containing customer content without explicit legal approval. Collect references (request-ids, traces) and ask Customer Success to notify impacted customers if required.
  - Use redwoodctl audit export --request-id <id> to pull event references only.

- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools):
  - Operators may have deeper node-level access; follow the EBS snapshot and KV cache export steps.
  - If the node is in a customer VPC, coordinate with customer/network team and obey contractual restrictions.

- Private deployments (VPC / on-prem):
  - Follow customer-approved forensic procedures; obtain customer consent if required by contract.
  - When evidence must remain on-prem for legal/regulatory reasons, document chain-of-custody handoff and store a signed manifest copy in evidence-bucket (metadata-only) for Redwood records.

Query examples for correlating events
- Audit-collector (KQL example):
  audit.action: "model.pull" AND audit.user: "svc-deploy-*" AND @timestamp:[2026-05-03T13:00:00 TO 2026-05-03T15:00:00]

- Network egress (AWS VPC flow logs filter):
  aws_account=123456789012 AND dstport=443 AND dstaddr in [list of suspicious IPs] AND start_time BETWEEN '2026-05-03T13:00:00Z' AND '2026-05-03T15:00:00Z'

- Example SQL for trace joins (analytics DB):
  SELECT t.request_id, t.user_id, s.session_id, s.commands
  FROM traces t
  JOIN sessions s ON t.session_id = s.session_id
  WHERE t.request_time BETWEEN '2026-05-03 13:00:00' AND '2026-05-03 15:00:00'

Escalation & disclosure guidance
- If sensitive customer data was exposed, IC must notify Legal and Customer Success within 4 hours of confirmation.
- Follow the incident disclosure checklist (see related page /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/incident-evidence-orchestration-for-multi-tenant-model-failures-2026) for public/regulated disclosures.

Evidence handling flow diagram (textual)
1. Detect -> 2. Contain -> 3. Live capture -> 4. Snapshot/export -> 5. Upload to evidence-bucket -> 6. Generate manifest & sign -> 7. Legal review & hold -> 8. Analysis & report -> 9. Close or escalate to regulatory body

Audit and logging retention alignment
- Ensure the audit-collector retains raw logs for at least 90 days by default; extend to 2 years for incidents with evidence retained longer.
- Correlate evidence-bucket access logs with the audit-collector export to demonstrate who accessed artifacts and when.

Appendices
A. Forensics quick commands
- Export OpenSearch documents to JSON: `curl -XPOST "https://audit-collector/_search?scroll=1m&size=1000" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query": {...}}' > audit-export.json`
- Copy to evidence-bucket: `aws s3 cp audit-export.json s3://redwood-evidence-prod/incidents/INC-2026-045/audit-export.json`

B. Minimal preservation checklist (copy into incident ticket)
- [ ] Session terminated or isolated
- [ ] Audit logs exported for window T-1h..T+1h
- [ ] Node snapshots created (EBS or filesystem)
- [ ] KV cache export saved
- [ ] Manifest created and signed
- [ ] Artifacts uploaded to evidence-bucket with checksums
- [ ] Legal informed and hold decision recorded

C. Contacts (oncall rotation)
- Security oncall (IC): security-oncall@redwood.ai
- Forensics team pager: +1-555-0102 (pager)
- Runtime owner slack: #eng-runtime
- Legal emergency: legal@redwood.ai (pager-enabled)
